english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: Carpenter, my loom leans. I will set up a loom of birch in your house. Will it stand straight? It will stand straight. What will you weave on it? My sons' garments. Then weave me one too, and I will take no wage. With joy!

english: Carpenter, the wheel of my wagon is split. Did the axle break too? The axle is whole. Then drive the wagon to my house. I will cut a new wheel from an oak. Will it be strong? It will be stronger than the old one. Make it quickly; the harvest time is coming. Then I will work through the night.

english: Carpenter, my old yoke has broken. My oxen are standing in the field. Who made it? My father made it. It was weak. I will carve a new one out of a beech. Then I will rub it with a stone and bore through it with an awl. When will you complete it? Wait three nights, then come. I will bring you a lamb.

pie: tétḱon moy h₂érh₃trom h₂éǵroy bʰidtó. uksn̥bʰís h₂érh₃yes h₁éḱwoh₁-wē h₂érh₃yes? uksn̥bʰís. ḱuh₁róm dukénti. tóy ḱuh₁rṓs h₂érh₃trom-kʷe sénom h₁ést. h₂érh₃trom toy bʰeh₂ǵṓd péyḱoh₂. h₁íd moḱs h₂réydʰe wésni séh₁yoh₂. h₂éti h₂ewsér gʷm̥dʰí.
english: Carpenter, my plough split in the field. Were you ploughing with oxen or with a horse? With oxen. They pull strongly. They are strong, and the plough was old. I will carve you a plough of beech. Make it ready quickly; in spring I sow. Come back at dawn.

pie: gʷḗn ḱóm kʷérom spéḱye. h₂Hséh₂i moy bʰidtó. wódr̥ h₁ésmi h₁én h₁ést? wódr̥ ne h₁ést. pótnih₂ moy h₁ím gʷʰermóysu h₁n̥gʷl̥sú dʰéh₁t. nu péh₂wr̥ h₁ím bʰéydt. ǵʰóstoh₁ moy h₁ím dʰinǵʰtā́m. h₂élyom moy dʰinǵʰdʰí gʰéldʰōh₂-kʷe toy. h₁ím dʰinéǵʰoh₂. wódr̥ h₁ím h₁n̥dó ǵʰudʰí.
english: Woman, look at this pot! It split on my hearth. Was there water in it? There was no water. My wife set it on the hot embers. Then the fire split it. My hands shaped it. Shape me another, and I will pay you. I will shape it. Pour water into it!

english: Neighbour, what are you doing with that earth? I am shaping pots. I dry them in the sun. Then I burn them in the fire. Does the fire not break them? It breaks a few. The good ones are hard. Sell me a hard one. What will you give me? Salt. I carry salt from the salt marsh. Salt is dear to me. Take it.

pie: ǵérh₂ont moy toy méǵistom wérǵom wéwke. h₃rēǵéy kʷérom kʷérm̥. ḱm̥tóm wiHrṓs dh₂pnóy h₁ésmōd ph₃ént. ḱm̥tóm wiHrṓs. déms méǵyōs h₁ést? ne h₁ést. h₁éḱwōd méǵyōs h₁ést. nu kúdʰe h₁éy h₁ésti? póyḱōs h₁ím h₁r̥h₁pyónt. nu nos h₃rēǵéy h₂élyom wr̥ǵdʰí. h₁eǵóh₂ ǵérh₂onts ǵʰóstoh₁ moy ḱm̥h₂tā́m.
english: Old man, tell me about your greatest work. I made a cauldron for the king. A hundred men drank from it at the feast. A hundred men! Was it bigger than a house? It was not. It was bigger than a horse. Where is it now? Enemies carried it off. Then make another for our king! I am old; my hands have grown tired.

pie: kʷíd moy wíHre h₂éydʰom gʷm̥yési? gʷéru moy kh₃téwi Hruptó. néweh₂m moy h₂éyesos h₂éḱih₂m kʷr̥dʰí. kúdʰe séneh₂ h₂éḱih₂ h₁ésti? néḱt tworḱóy-kʷe ménet. nu h₂éyos wéḱmi h₂éyos-kʷe polh₁ú h₂élgʷʰeti. kʷíd dédeh₃esi? tworḱósyo dénḱtreh₂ swéh₂m-kʷe skéwHtim. téh₂ h₁époh₂.
english: Warrior, why do you come to my fire? My spear broke in the fight. Make me a new point of bronze. Where is the old point? It was lost; it stayed in the boar. Then I need bronze, and bronze is worth much. What will you give? The boar's fangs and its hide. I will take them.

english: Daughter, winter is coming, and I am cold. Grandfather, I will sew you a garment from the hides of sheep. Leave the wool on the hides! I will leave it. The wool will warm you. What shall I give you? Tell me a story by the hearth. I will tell you the story of the wolf and the bear.

english: My oxen are slow. I want a sharp pointed tool. Shall I make it from bronze or from horn? From horn. Bronze costs much. Find me the horn of a stag. Will they not become angry? They will become angry. They will walk more swiftly.

english: Of-Goodly-Fame, I have come from the river. I will give you fish for a blade. Fish rot. Show me something else. Then I will give you fish and salt. Salt! Now you speak wisely. How many loads of salt do you have? Two loads. Bring them, and take the blade.

english: Friend, I will pay you grain for a hide. How many loads will you pay? Two loads. Two loads are few. This hide is thick. Give three loads, and take the hide. Three loads, then. Stretch out your right hand. I give you my right hand. Bring the grain at dawn.

english: Kindly one, I give back your awl. It broke in my hand. My good awl! What did you do with it? I bored through a hard bone. An awl does not bore through bone; it bores through hide. Whoever breaks a pointed tool, let him pay the penalty. I will give you a new awl and a cup of mead. Then you are still dear to me.

english: Of-True-Fame, we are preparing a feast for my daughter at harvest time. I want ten cups. Ten cups! Will you have so many guests? All the village will come. Then I will shape the cups from the earth of the river and burn them for three days. May they be beautiful! My cups are the most beautiful in the village. That is a boast! Show me one.

english: Neighbour, why are you angry? Your dog ran among my cups and broke them. My dog? He was sleeping by the hearth. I saw him with my eyes. Then I will pay. What do you want? Four lambs. That is much! I will give you two lambs. Three lambs, and tie up your dog!

english: I am going a long way. I have need of a bag. Shall I sew a big one or a small one? A big one. I will carry grain and thick milk in it. Then I will sew two hides together with sinew. Who are you? Where are you going? I am a shepherd. I am going to my brother. May the gods guard you on the road!

english: I milk my cows in the morning. My hollow vessel is split. I will hollow you a vessel out of birch. Why do you choose birch? Birch is soft, and it does not smell. english: Old man, my comb vanished in the river. Did I shape it from bone, or from horn? From horn. My mother gave it to me. I remember. I made it for her. Make me a new one. Bring me the horn of a stag. I have no horn. My husband hunts in the mountains; he will kill one.

english: Old friend, my spear is not straight. Show it to me. I will straighten it over the fire. Will the fire not burn it? I heat it; I do not burn it. Warm wood is soft. Who taught you this? My uncle, a wise carpenter.

english: Why is your fire small today? The bellows are old, and my son is sleeping. Take the bellows and push them! I am a guest! Shall the guest work? Here the guest works, and he eats. See! The embers are red. Now I strike the bronze on the anvil.
